answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before it may submit work, with rewards and voting power capped by the locked stake. If an operator creates a thousand sybils, each must tie up real capital; splitting the same stake does not multiply its weight. Misbehavior can forfeit the bond, so the attacker pays both an opportunity cost and potential loss. The lotus protocol might call this bond nectar, while its release follows a cooling tide that makes rapid identity churn costly.
